subsystems.name: Atmospheric thickening
subsystems.role: raise surface pressure enough to allow liquid water and reduce the need for pressure suits.

subsystems.name: Radiation shielding
subsystems.role: protect the surface from cosmic rays and solar particles.
parts: artificial magnetic field at a Lagrange point

subsystems.name: Biological succession
subsystems.role: introduce photosynthetic life to generate oxygen and soil.

subsystems.name: Monitoring and control
subsystems.role: manage the planet-wide system over centuries.

buildSteps.title: Survey and model
buildSteps.detail: Map the planet's frozen volatiles and run climate models to estimate how much CO2, water and nitrogen are available. Studies disagree on whether Mars holds enough CO2 for a breathable atmosphere.

buildSteps.title: Warm the poles
buildSteps.detail: Use orbital mirrors or release engineered greenhouse gases to raise polar temperatures, sublimating CO2 ice and starting a warming feedback.

buildSteps.title: Thicken the atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Continue warming to release more CO2 and add synthetic greenhouse gases. Pressure rises from less than 1% of Earth's to perhaps tens of kilopascals.

buildSteps.title: Add water
buildSteps.detail: Melt subsurface and polar ice; if needed, redirect comets or icy asteroids to deliver more water. Liquid water becomes stable in low-lying regions.

buildSteps.title: Shield from radiation
buildSteps.detail: Place a magnetic shield at the Mars–Sun Lagrange point to deflect solar wind, or accept higher radiation and build underground.

buildSteps.title: Seed life
buildSteps.detail: Introduce photosynthetic cyanobacteria and engineered microbes to fix carbon and nitrogen, slowly building soil and releasing oxygen.

buildSteps.title: Build a breathable atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Over centuries, oxygen accumulates. The mix is managed to avoid runaway greenhouse or toxic levels.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and stabilize
buildSteps.detail: A permanent monitoring and control system manages the new climate.

prerequisites.why: No technology exists to alter a whole planet's atmosphere; only models and small-scale experiments.
Robotic missions have made oxygen and water from regolith, but not at industrial scale.
Space stations recycle air and water, but not yet at the scale or reliability of a city.
We can send tonnes, not the millions of tonnes required to import volatiles.
Microbes can be engineered for extreme conditions, but none are proven for Mars.

pathway.milestone: robotic orbiters and rovers map volatiles and climate
